steps.stdout:
Link the project to a Gitea repository, or link it again to move it.

The server checks the token reaches the repository before storing the
link, and answers with the integration it saved — including the webhook
URL Gitea should post events to, and its secret when the key may see it.

--token may be left out to keep the stored token, which only works while
the base URL is the saved integration's; a new instance or repository
needs a token. Connecting again with a different repository or instance
is how the link is moved — update only changes the two settings.

Usage:
  kaneo integration gitea connect <owner>/<repository> [flags]

Flags:
      --base-url string   the Gitea instance's URL, e.g. https://gitea.example.com
  -h, --help              help for connect
      --token string      the Gitea access token; only - is accepted, which reads it from stdin

Global Flags:
      --api-key string     API key; prefer KANEO_API_KEY, since a flag is visible in the process list
      --api-url string     Kaneo base URL (env KANEO_API_URL)
      --human              force human-readable output, even through a pipe
      --jq string          filter JSON output with a jq expression (implies --json)
      --json               force JSON output
  -p, --project string     project id, slug or name (env KANEO_PROJECT)
      --timeout duration   per-request timeout (default 10s)
  -w, --workspace string   workspace id, slug or name (env KANEO_WORKSPACE)
